newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil rebounds in late active trade.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil rebounds in late active trade.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL
Mar (3rd pos) 1,238 rgt/tonne Dec (south) 1,260
Open/Hi/Low 1,235/1,244/1,228 Prev close 1,255
Prev settlement 1,232 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices closed higher on late covering due to expectation of demand and ahead of bullish December data by SGS (M) Bhd and Ivan Wong. Trading remained volatile with prices easing earlier on profit-taking and technical adjustment. March futures's support 1,230 and resistance 1,250
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Interest was seen among nearby CPOS. Players are waiting for fresh developments.
Palm oil in Malaysia rebounded in late trading and closed higher after easing earlier due to technical adjustments, traders said.
"The market saw some covering and technical buying after March futures rose above the 1,235 ringgit," a trader said.
At the close, the contract was up six ringgit at 1,238 ringgit ($490.29) a tonne. March futures contract next resistance will be 1,250 and support at 1,230.
"We have to wait for more developments and fresh leads tomorrow to give the market a clearer path," a trader said.
"Prices rebounded after yesterday's brief downward correction," another trader said.
"The rise is expected as the underlying fundamental outlooks remain good in the near-term," he said.
However, price movements were limited to a tight range as players continued to wait for fresh developments.
The market is waiting for a crop report from forecaster Ivan Wong who is scheduled to release its fresh December crop estimates on exports/stocks/output on Friday.
Cargo surveyor SGS (M) Sdn Bhd will announce December 1-20 palm oil exports on Friday to provide the market a lead.
Some covering emerged in the afternoonon epxectation of a bullish December 1-20 palm oil export, traders said.
On Monday SGS (M) Sdn Bhd estimated Malaysia's palm oil exports for December 1-15 at 406,924 tonnes compared with 298,862 tonnes for November 1-15.
They said expectation of lower output in coming months, because of the seasonal downtrend, could see prices rise further in near-term.
Feb (south) was offered at 1,260 and bids at 1,252.50.
Among refined products, Jan RBD palm oil was offered at $532.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia, and Feb/March at $530.
Jan RBD palm olein saw offers at $570, Feb/March at $565 and Apr/May/June at $557.50.
Jan RBD palm stearin was offered at $400, Feb/Mar at $405, and Jan/Feb palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $292.50.
